title: A Geometric Information Bottleneck for Activation Steering

problem.claim: Activation-based steering can cause broad, entangled behavioral changes that unintentionally alter unrelated capabilities.

gap.claim: Existing steering reliability is limited for fine-grained behavioral control.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes IB-ACT, a disentanglement-based intervention framework that identifies where and how to intervene using layer-wise representation geometry.
IB-ACT selects layers before intervention and applies geometrically constrained transformations to behavior-relevant activation subspaces while preserving orthogonal structure.
The paper provides an IB-style theoretical justification that interventions at selected layers reduce unintended information leakage.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report consistent empirical improvements over recent baselines on toxicity control and hallucination reduction.
The authors analyze the spectral structure of behavior-relevant representations for jailbreak mitigation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Activation steering may unintentionally change unrelated model capabilities.
The paper reframes behavioral intervention as a geometric information bottleneck problem.
IB-ACT uses layer-wise geometry to isolate behavior-relevant information and determine intervention location and form.
The paper gives an IB-style theoretical account of reduced unintended information leakage.
The authors report improvements on toxicity control and hallucination reduction and argue that structurally appropriate layer selection is important for disentangled steering.

source_observation.claim: The method targets behavior-relevant subspaces while preserving orthogonal representational structure.

interpretation.claim: Constraining interventions according to representation geometry may help reduce collateral behavioral changes.

application.claim: For fine-grained steering, inspect layer-wise representation geometry before choosing intervention layers and target subspaces.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the evaluated toxicity-control and hallucination-reduction settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, metrics, quantitative results, or baseline identities.
The abstract does not provide the layer-selection criterion, intervention parameters, or theoretical assumptions.
The abstract does not report implementation details or independent verification.
